events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday during high tides in the late
mornings.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur in the
late mornings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal residents and managers of
infrastructure in the warned area should prepare for rising
water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property. High tides each day will occur in the late morning.
Observed high tides are 1.5 to 1.7 feet above astronomical
tide predictions.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Rio Arriba, NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 PM MDT Monday the stage was 6.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:00 PM MDT Monday was 6.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
Tuesday morning and continue falling to 4.5 feet through
Wednesday.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.5
feet on 08/06/2006.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Areas of fog will continue overnight over most of northeastern
Wyoming and western South Dakota.

Patchy dense fog will occur through sunrise. With temperatures
near freezing, elevated surfaces such as overpasses and bridges
may become slick.

Motorists should expect rapidly changing visibility, down to near
zero at times. Remember to use your low beam headlights in fog,
slow down, and provide plenty of braking distance between yourself
and any vehicles in front of you.

events.summary:

will move inland over the southwest quadrant of PR shortly. Expect

Lajas County in Puerto Rico...
Sabana Grande County in Puerto Rico...
San German County in Puerto Rico...
Yauco County in Puerto Rico...

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.

Yauco, San German, Lajas, Sabana Grande, Guanica, Hormigueros,

Torres, Sabana Eneas, La Parguera, Lluveras, Fuig, Betances,

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Up to 2.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, and 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39
PM Friday 10/30. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
